title: Escalation: Tenant burst causes intermittent 5xx/timeouts — implement selective fast-fail quarantine and graceful retry policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A high-volume tenant experienced a sudden upload/streaming burst that amplified client retries and triggered proxy connection hold behavior, causing a cascade of 5xx responses and timeouts across the Hosted API. This ticket implements a staged mitigation: (1) selective fast-fail (tenant-scoped quarantine) to prevent overload, (2) an adaptive retry quarantine policy communicated via headers, and (3) telemetry changes to measure request amplification and retry loops. Goal: stop immediate customer-visible 5xx waves and provide safe gradable rollout to avoid collateral degradation.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate tenant burst: 1000 concurrent streaming requests with variable chunk sizes (1-8 requests/sec per connection) targeting hosted inference endpoint
Enable aggressive client-side retries (exponential backoff with no jitter) to mimic SDK misconfiguration
Observe edge proxy connection queue growth, backend KV cache thrashing, inflated in-flight requests, and 5xx rates in /metrics/hosted-api/5xx by tenant
Reproduce in staging with tenant-scoped rate override to validate fast-fail logic
implementation_notes: Fast-fail quarantine: add a tenant admission controller that flips to QUARANTINED on surge signal (thresholds: sustained 95th p99 queue depth > X for Y seconds). When QUARANTINED, new requests return 429/499-like structured response with Retry-After and X-Redwood-Quarantine-Token header for transparent client handling.

Adaptive retry policy: update gateway to set X-Client-Retry-Hint header containing recommended retry strategy (backoff base, max attempts) for SDKs; implement server-side ephemeral dedupe for same idempotency token to avoid processing duplicates.
Connection admission: limit per-tenant concurrent streaming sessions and cap per-connection request rate, with graceful draining to avoid connection churn and backend overload.
KV cache prefetch/lock: during quarantine, reduce aggressive KV eviction by increasing soft TTL and enabling a small prefetch for hot prefixes to avoid cold-start fanout.
Observability: add tenant-scoped amplification metric (requests_received / unique_client_id) and a retry-loop detector tracing span to quickly identify misbehaving SDKs.

Rollout strategy: feature flag gated and staged by region then tenant size. Start with internal canary tenants -> low-risk customers -> broad rollout. Default OFF in Dedicated/Private clusters unless explicitly opted-in.
acceptance_criteria: No customer-visible 5xx spike in the next simulated burst test after feature is enabled for canary tenants
Quarantine header present and SDKs able to parse Retry-After and X-Client-Retry-Hint during canary
Telemetry surfaces amplification > 5x within 1m alerts to SRE (dashboard prepopulated)
Smoke tests for streaming, non-streaming, and embedding endpoints pass under quarantine policy
Documentation updated: Console runbook, SDK best-practices page, and customer-facing KB article draft
